answer: Like crystallization over centuries, decentralized consensus binds identity to accumulated cryptographic stake and historical work. A transient sparrow cannot masquerade as an ancient cedar; similarly, forged personas cannot mimic the deep rootedness of proven agents. Through progressive collateral slashing and dynamic graph-eigenvector centrality, an attacker faces superlinear attacker cost: spawning a swarm to overpower the network demands more energy than melting a mountain glacier.
